name: Sri Lanka
summary_text: Sri Lanka is dangerous for trans visitors. Sections 365/365A of the 1883 Penal Code criminalise same-sex activity (up to 10 years, applying to men and women), and Human Dignity Trust lists Sri Lanka as criminalising the gender expression of trans people: police use vagrancy and “cheating by personation” provisions against trans people. The International Commission of Jurists identifies Sri Lanka Police as “the foremost perpetrators of human rights violations against LGBTI individuals” — harassment, arbitrary detention, and abuse are documented as systematic, though formal prosecutions remain limited. There is no legal gender recognition (a 2016 recognition circular exists but is not law), no anti-discrimination protection, and no hate-crime statute. Colombo has a small organised community (EQUAL GROUND) and tourist areas are accustomed to foreigners, which moderates but does not remove risk: the realistic worst case is police harassment or detention under personation/vagrancy provisions rather than prosecution.

sources.title: Sri Lanka | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Sections 365/365A of the Penal Code criminalise same-sex activity (up to 10 years, applying to men and women); prosecutions limited but harassment, violence, extortion, arbitrary arrests and denial of services are frequent; no comprehensive anti-discrimination protections; authorities use forced anal and vaginal examinations to seek evidence - widely condemned as torture. Legal gender recognition is possible (via a certification process).
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Sri Lanka's criminalisation of same-sex activity.

sources.title: Sri Lanka: Protecting transgender persons: Going beyond rule by circular | ICJ
sources.claim_summary: ICJ opinion piece (Aug 2023) by Mathuri Thamilmaran: 'Protecting transgender persons: Going beyond rule by circular' - the Sri Lanka Police are the foremost perpetrators of human-rights violations against LGBTI individuals; recent months saw both the Police and the Human Rights Commission acknowledging this; argues administrative circulars are insufficient without legal reform.

UK Home Office CPIN Sri Lanka: Sexual orientation and gender identity or expression (v6.0, Sept 2024): assessment of risk from state and non-state actors, protection, internal relocation and certification for LGBT+ asylum claims, with detailed country information.

US State Department country report for Sri Lanka (custom URL): official human-rights assessment including the SOGI section - criminalisation under the penal code and police harassment of LGBT persons.

Joint UPR stakeholder report (EQUAL GROUND, Northwestern CIHR, GIHR) for Sri Lanka's 3rd cycle: 'Human Rights Violations Against LGBTIQ Individuals in Sri Lanka' - documents criminalisation and violations by the coalition of NGOs for UPR.

Canada IRB Response to Information Request LKA103948.E (Jan 2012): 'Treatment of sexual minorities in Sri Lanka' - Article 365 criminalises 'carnal intercourse against the order of nature' (up to 10 years, men only); Article 365A 'gross indecency' (both sexes, amended 1995 to cover women); rarely enforced with no convictions, but criminalisation 'paves the way for police and anti-gay groups to brand all lesbian, bisexual, transgendered persons as perverts and criminals'.
